lessons.title: Khadijah: the first to stand with him
lessons.intro: Learn how Khadijah comforted the Prophet ﷺ on the night of the first revelation, what he said about her, and how we can honour those we love.

steps.title: Khadijah: the best of the women of her time
body: Ali ibn Abi Talib heard the Prophet ﷺ say: “Mary, the daughter of Imran, was the best of the women of her time, and Khadijah is the best of the women of this nation” (Bukhari 3432; Muslim 2430 has the same words about the women “of her time”).
Khadijah bint Khuwaylid was the first wife of the Prophet ﷺ. She was with him when revelation began, and her words that day are among the best known in the sunnah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The night in the cave of Hira
body: Aisha told how revelation began. The Prophet ﷺ used to spend days in the cave of Hira in worship. One day the angel came and told him to read. He said three times that he could not read, and each time the angel pressed him hard and then released him. Then the angel recited the first words of Surat al-Alaq (Bukhari 3).

The Prophet ﷺ came home with his heart beating hard and said to Khadijah: “Cover me! Cover me!” They covered him until the fear passed. He told her everything and said: “I fear that something may happen to me” (Bukhari 3).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The first word revealed
steps.note: The first revelation began with the command iqra’, which means read, or recite. It is the first ayah of Surat al-Alaq.

steps.title: What Khadijah said
body: Khadijah did not tell him to calm down and forget it. She said: “Never! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep good relations with your kith and kin, help the poor and the destitute, serve your guests generously and assist the deserving calamity-afflicted ones” (Bukhari 3).

Then she took him to her cousin Waraqa ibn Nawfal, an old man who had become a Christian and wrote from the Gospel. Waraqa listened and said that this was the same angel Allah had sent to Moses, and that he wished he were young enough to support the Prophet ﷺ when his people drove him out (Bukhari 3).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Why her words mattered
body: Khadijah did not argue about what the angel was. She answered from what she knew of him: his kindness to family, to the poor and the guest, and to people in trouble. Her reasoning was that a man like that is not left to fail.
This is a lesson in how to support someone who is afraid. First she listened. Then she reminded him of the good in him. Then she took him to someone who could help.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: The greeting from her Lord
body: Abu Huraira reported that Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “This is Khadijah coming to you with a dish of food or drink. When she reaches you, greet her from her Lord and from me, and give her the good news of a house in Paradise of hollow pearl, in which there will be neither noise nor toil” (Bukhari 3820; Muslim 2432 has the same news of a palace of jewels).

The Arabic of the report uses a word for the house whose exact meaning the narrators explain differently, so the translations vary: palace, house of pearl, hollow pearl. What is clear is the greeting and the good news.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The word qasab in Bukhari 3820 is translated in different ways. The wording here follows the corpus and says that translations vary. Please confirm.

steps.title: He never forgot her
body: Aisha said she never felt as jealous of any wife of the Prophet ﷺ as she did of Khadijah, though she never saw her, because he mentioned her so often. Whenever he slaughtered a sheep he would cut it up and send parts to Khadijah’s women friends (Bukhari 3818).
When Aisha said it was as if there was no woman on earth but Khadijah, he said: “Her love had been nurtured in my heart by Allah Himself” (Muslim 2435).
Khadijah died three years before he married Aisha (Muslim 2435). Years later he still honoured her and her friends.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What the seerah books add
body: The seerah books (Ibn Hisham, quoting Ibn Ishaq) report that Khadijah was a businesswoman of Quraysh who hired men to trade with her wealth, that she was among the first to believe in the Prophet ﷺ, and that she supported him so that, when he came home, what grieved him eased.
These are seerah reports and are not taken from the six hadith books. They have not yet been checked by a scholar for this app, so hold them as reports and not as established facts.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.source: Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya, vol. 1 pp. 188, 240 (seerah; not from the six books)
steps.review: Seerah-only claims (her trade, being among the first to believe, her support). Please confirm or remove.

steps.text: Remember them often, and speak well of them.
Be kind to their friends and family, even years later.
steps.detail: He sent meat to her friends (Bukhari 3818).

steps.text: When a loved one is afraid, listen first.
steps.detail: She let him tell her everything (Bukhari 3).

steps.text: Remind them of the good in them.
Take them to someone who can help.
Make dua for those who have died.

lessons.title: Asiya: faith in the tyrant’s house
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an says about Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh: her words for the baby Musa and her dua for a house near Allah.

steps.title: A believer in the house of the tyrant
body: Asiya was the wife of Pharaoh, the ruler who claimed to be a lord. The Qur’an gives her as an example for every believer: “And Allah presents an example of those who believed: the wife of Pharaoh” (66:11).
She lived in the most dangerous house of her time, and kept her faith. This lesson shows what she said and what she asked of Allah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The baby in the river
body: Allah inspired the mother of Musa to put her baby in the river when she feared for him (28:7). The family of Pharaoh picked him up (28:8).
Then the wife of Pharaoh said: “[He will be] a comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son.” And they perceived not (28:9).
The Qur’an does not say what she knew at that moment. It says what she said, and that Allah’s plan was working in a place no one could see.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What her words show
body: In a house where children were killed, she spoke up for one baby. She called him a comfort of the eye, which is a way of saying he is a joy to look at. She asked that he not be killed, and said they might adopt him.
The verse does not say whether Pharaoh agreed because of her words or for another reason. It says she spoke, and Musa was raised in that house.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The explanation that “comfort of the eye” means joy to look at is the usual explanation of the phrase. Please confirm.

steps.title: Her dua
steps.note: This is the ayah that records her prayer. She asked for a house near Allah in Paradise, and for rescue from Pharaoh, his deeds and the wrongdoing people.

steps.title: The order of her prayer
body: Look at what she asked first: “build for me near You a house in Paradise.” She asked for nearness to Allah before she asked to be saved (66:11).

Then she asked three things in one breath: be saved from Pharaoh, from his deeds, and from the wrongdoing people. She did not only ask to escape the man, but also the deeds and the way of life around her.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: What the Prophet ﷺ said of her
body: Abu Musa al-Ashari reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Many men reached perfection, but among women none reached it except Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, and Mary, the daughter of Imran. And the excellence of Aisha over other women is like the excellence of tharid over other food” (Bukhari 3411; Bukhari 3769).
Asiya is named with Maryam, and in the Qur’an they are paired as examples (66:11-12).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What we do not know
body: Many stories about Asiya are told in books and videos: how she died, what Pharaoh did, what she saw. The Qur’an does not tell us those things, and the sound hadith we checked do not either.
So in this lesson we say only what Allah and the Prophet ﷺ said. The rest is not claimed, and if you hear it, you can say you do not know.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Many accounts of Asiya’s death exist in books of tafsir. None is in the Qur’an or the six books as far as we checked. Please confirm that the lesson may leave them out.

steps.title: Praying like Asiya

steps.text: Start by asking for nearness to Allah.
Then name what you need to be saved from.
Ask for the deeds and the surroundings that harm you to be removed, not only the person.
If you can, speak up for the weak near you.
Trust Allah’s plan even when you cannot see it.

steps.intro: A dua for anyone in a hard place: at work, at school or at home.
mistakes: Praying only to be rescued, and never for nearness to Allah.
Thinking you must leave the place at once before you can be a believer. Asiya was a believer in her house.
steps.label: [Reflection]

lessons.title: Maryam: the palm tree
lessons.intro: Follow the story of Maryam in the Qur’an: her worship, the news, the palm tree and the baby who spoke.

steps.title: Chosen above the women of the worlds
body: The angels said to Maryam: “O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds” (3:42). She is the only woman named in the Qur’an, and the nineteenth surah carries her name.
The Prophet ﷺ said that Mary, the daughter of Imran, was the best of the women of her time (Bukhari 3432). In this lesson you will follow her from the prayer chamber to the palm tree.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Provision in the prayer chamber
body: Allah put Maryam in the care of Zakariya. “Every time Zechariah entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. He said, «O Mary, from where is this [coming] to you?» She said, «It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account»” (3:37).
She had grown up in worship, and she knew where her provision came from.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The inner speech is marked with « » so that it can be matched to the verse. Please confirm the format.

steps.title: The news
body: She withdrew from her family to a place toward the east. Allah sent His angel to her as a well-proportioned man (19:16-17). She said: «Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, [so leave me], if you should be fearing of Allah» (19:18).

He said: «I am only the messenger of your Lord to give you [news of] a pure boy» (19:19). She asked how she could have a boy when no man had touched her (19:20). He answered that her Lord says it is easy for Him, and that He will make the boy a sign to the people and a mercy from Him (19:21).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Her first words were a refuge
body: When a stranger appeared, her first act was to seek refuge in Allah. She did not argue with him or try to out-talk him. She called on the Most Merciful and reminded him to fear Allah.
When she learned that the visitor was Allah’s messenger, she asked her question honestly, and she was answered honestly.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: The palm tree
body: The pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said: «Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten» (19:23). Allah did not rebuke her for it. A voice from below her said: «Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream» (19:24).
It also told her: «shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates. So eat and drink and be contented» (19:25-26).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Shake the trunk
body: A woman in labour was told to shake a palm tree. She could hardly do it, and still Allah told her to do what she could, and promised the dates.
Many scholars have noted this: provision comes with a small effort, even when you are weak. It is not a ruling, it is a lesson.
steps.label: [Reflection]
steps.review: The comment that scholars have noted the lesson of effort is common in tafsir but is not sourced here. Please confirm or remove.

steps.title: The baby who spoke
body: She brought the baby to her people, and they said: «O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented» (19:27). She pointed to him. They said: «How can we speak to one who is in the cradle a child?» (19:29).
The baby said: «Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I am» (19:30-31). Her defence was her son’s voice.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Described by Allah
body: Allah describes Maryam in the Qur’an: “his mother was a supporter of truth” (5:75). And: “she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures and was of the devoutly obedient” (66:12).
Allah also says that He made her and her son a sign for the worlds (21:91).
steps.label: [Established]

mistakes: Waiting for a miracle and doing nothing.
Arguing with people who accuse you, instead of showing the truth.

lessons.title: Hajar: she ran seven times
lessons.intro: Learn the story of Hajar and Zamzam from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, how it became part of Hajj, and what trust in Allah looks like.

steps.title: The mother of Ismail
body: Hajar (Hagar) was the wife of Ibrahim and the mother of Ismail. The Qur’an does not tell her story by name, but the Prophet ﷺ did, in a long report that Ibn Abbas narrated (Bukhari 3364).
Her walk between two hills is remembered in the Hajj and Umrah every year. This lesson tells the story from that report and shows what it asks of us.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Left in an empty valley
body: Ibrahim brought Hajar and her baby Ismail to a place near where the Ka’bah would be, under a tree. There was nobody in Makkah and no water. He left them with a leather bag of dates and a small water-skin, and turned to go (Bukhari 3364).

She followed him and said: “O Ibrahim! Where are you going, leaving us in this valley where there is no person whose company we may enjoy, nor anything?” She said it many times, and he did not look back. Then she asked: “Has Allah ordered you to do so?” He said: “Yes.” She said: “Then He will not neglect us” (Bukhari 3364).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Then He will not neglect us
body: Her first questions came from fear and love. Her last sentence came from trust. When she knew that it was Allah’s order, she accepted it and went back to her baby.
This is tawakkul: the fear does not disappear, but it no longer rules.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: The dua of Ibrahim
body: Out of sight, Ibrahim faced the Ka’bah and raised his hands. He prayed: “Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they might be grateful” (14:37; Bukhari 3364).
He asked for prayer first, then for hearts to incline to them, then for food.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Between Safa and Marwa
body: The water ran out. The child was thirsty and suffering. She could not bear to watch, so she went to Safa, the nearest hill, and looked for anyone. She saw no one. She came down to the valley, tucked up her robe and ran like a person in distress until she crossed the valley and reached Marwa. She repeated this seven times (Bukhari 3364).
The Prophet ﷺ said: “This is the source of the tradition of the walking of people between them (Safa and Marwa)” (Bukhari 3364).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The water
body: When she reached Marwa for the last time, she heard a voice. She said: “O, whoever you may be! You have made me hear your voice; have you got something to help me?” She saw an angel at the place of Zamzam, digging the earth with his heel (or his wing) until water flowed (Bukhari 3364).

She made a basin around it with her hand and filled her water-skin. The Prophet ﷺ said: “May Allah bestow mercy on Ismail’s mother! Had she let Zamzam flow (or had she not scooped from it), it would have been a stream flowing on the surface of the earth.” Then she drank and nursed her child (Bukhari 3364).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What the angel said
body: The angel told her: “Do not be afraid of being neglected, for this is the House of Allah which will be built by this boy and his father, and Allah never neglects His people” (Bukhari 3364).

Later, a family of the tribe of Jurhum saw birds circling and found the water. They asked her if they could stay with her, and she said they could, but they would have no right to the water. They agreed (Bukhari 3364).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: In the Qur’an
body: Allah says: “Indeed, as-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs ʿumrah, there is no blame upon him for walking between them” (2:158).
So the run of one mother has become part of the worship of millions of people.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The sa’i in the schools

rows.name: Shafi’i, Maliki and Hanbali
rows.text: The walking between Safa and Marwa (sa’i) is a pillar (rukn) of Hajj and Umrah. The Hajj or Umrah is not complete without it.

rows.name: Hanafi
rows.text: The sa’i is a required act (wajib), not a pillar. If a person leaves it, the Hajj is valid but he owes a sacrifice (dam).

steps.intro: All four schools agree that sa’i is part of Hajj and Umrah.
steps.agree: All four schools agree that it is seven trips, starting at Safa and ending at Marwa.
steps.closing: If you are going on Hajj or Umrah, follow your school and ask your guide.
steps.review: The ruling on sa’i in the four schools is stated from the usual teaching. Please confirm each row.
steps.label: [Interpretive]

steps.title: When you feel left alone

steps.text: Say what you feel. Hajar spoke to Ibrahim and asked.
Ask whether it is Allah’s command or a matter of fear.
Then say: “Then He will not neglect us”.
Do all you can, and go back to the task.
Do not take control of what Allah gives. Use it with thanks.

mistakes: Giving up trying because Allah is in control.

lessons.title: Aisha: the slander and the verdict
lessons.intro: Learn the story of the slander against Aisha from Bukhari 4750, how Allah declared her innocence and what we learn about rumours.

steps.title: Aisha, the daughter of Abu Bakr
body: Aisha was the daughter of Abu Bakr and a wife of the Prophet ﷺ. Allah says of his wives that they are “in the position of” the mothers of the believers (33:6), so she is called Umm al-Mu’minin.

Before the marriage, the Prophet ﷺ told her that she had been shown to him twice in a dream: a piece of silk with her picture, and a voice saying “this is your wife.” He said: “If this is from Allah, it will be done” (Bukhari 3895).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The most beloved, and a teacher
body: Amr ibn al-As asked the Prophet ﷺ: “Who is the most beloved person to you?” He said: “Aisha.” Amr asked, “Among the men?” He said: “Her father” (Bukhari 3662).
He also said that the excellence of Aisha over other women is like the excellence of tharid over other food (Bukhari 3769; Muslim 2446). Tharid is a dish of bread in broth that Arabs loved.

Abu Musa al-Ashari said: “Never was a hadith unclear to us, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, and we asked Aisha, except that we found some knowledge about it with her” (Tirmidhi 3883, sahih per al-Albani). Senior Companions came to a woman to ask about the religion.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Bukhari 3662, 3769; Muslim 2446; Tirmidhi 3883, sahih per al-Albani (sahih per al-Albani)

steps.title: Left behind
body: On a journey, Aisha went a little way from the camp. Her necklace broke and she went back to look for it. When she returned the army had moved on, and the men who carried her howdah thought she was inside it. She sat where she had been and fell asleep (Bukhari 4750).

Safwan ibn al-Muattil, who had stayed behind the army, found her in the morning. He said only “Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji’un”, made his camel kneel, and walked leading her to the army. Aisha says he did not say another word to her (Bukhari 4750).
Then the slander began, led by Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul (Bukhari 4750).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A month of waiting
body: Aisha fell ill for a month and did not know what people were saying. What worried her was that the Prophet ﷺ was no longer as kind to her as he used to be in sickness. He would come, greet her, say “How is that lady?” and leave (Bukhari 4750).

She learned of the slander from Umm Mistah. She asked to go to her parents, and wept all night. The Prophet ﷺ asked Usama, who said “we know nothing about her except good”, and Ali, who said that Barira, her servant, would tell the truth. Barira said she had never seen anything wrong in her, except that she was young and sometimes slept and left the dough uncovered (Bukhari 4750).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The revelation
body: The Prophet ﷺ sat with her and said: if you are innocent, Allah will declare your innocence; if you committed a sin, ask Allah’s forgiveness and repent, for Allah accepts the repentance of a slave who confesses and repents (Bukhari 4750).

Her parents did not know what to say. She said that she would speak as Yaqub, Yusuf’s father, did: “patience is most fitting”, and that Allah is the one sought for help (12:18). Then revelation came to the Prophet ﷺ, and when it passed he smiled and said: “Aisha, Allah has declared your innocence” (Bukhari 4750).
Her mother said to her, “Get up and go to him.” She said: “By Allah, I will not go to him, and I will not thank anybody but Allah” (Bukhari 4750). Allah revealed Surat an-Nur 24:11-20 on this matter.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The words Aisha chose
steps.note: Aisha did not remember the name of Yaqub, but she remembered his words when his sons lied to him. These words are from this ayah.

steps.title: What Allah taught about rumours
body: Allah asks: “Why, when you heard it, did not the believing men and believing women think good of one another and say, «This is an obvious falsehood»?” (24:12). And: “why, when you heard it, did you not say, «It is not for us to speak of this. Exalted are You, [O Allah]; this is a great slander»?” (24:16).
Allah also says that those who like immorality to be publicized among the believers will have a painful punishment (24:19).
So the Qur’an asks us to think well of believers, to ask for proof, and not to repeat what we have no knowledge of.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Abu Bakr and Mistah
body: Mistah ibn Uthatha was a poor relative of Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr used to support him. After he spread the slander, Abu Bakr swore he would never give him anything again (Bukhari 4750).

Then Allah revealed: “Would you not like that Allah should forgive you?” (24:22). Abu Bakr said: “Yes, by Allah, I wish that Allah should forgive me.” He resumed giving Mistah what he had given before, and said he would never stop it (Bukhari 4750).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A witness who spoke only what she knew
body: The Prophet ﷺ also asked Zaynab bint Jahsh, one of his wives who was close to Aisha in rank. She said: “I protect my hearing and my sight. I know nothing but good about Aisha.” Aisha said that Zaynab was her rival for his favour, yet Allah protected her because of her piety (Bukhari 4750).
Zaynab’s sister Hamna did spread the slander, and was among those who were harmed by it (Bukhari 4750).

lessons.title: Fatima: a part of him
lessons.intro: Learn what the sound reports tell us about Fatima, the daughter of the Prophet ﷺ: how he treated her, the secret she kept, and her words when he died.

steps.title: Fatima, daughter of the Prophet ﷺ
body: Fatima was the daughter of the Prophet ﷺ and Khadijah. Al-Miswar ibn Makhrama heard him say: “Fatima is a part of me, and he who makes her angry makes me angry” (Bukhari 3714). In Muslim 2449 he adds: “He in fact tortures me who tortures her.”
The sound reports tell us how he treated her, what he told her in his last illness, and what she said when he died.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: They stood up for each other
body: Aisha said: “I never saw anyone more like the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in gravity, calm and pleasant disposition... than Fatima.” When Fatima came to visit him, he stood up to welcome her, took her by the hand, kissed her and seated her where he had been sitting. When he visited her, she stood up, took him by the hand, kissed him and seated him in her place (Abu Dawud 5217, sahih per al-Albani).
So the Prophet ﷺ rose for his daughter, and she rose for him.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Abu Dawud 5217, sahih per al-Albani (sahih per al-Albani)

steps.title: The cloak
body: Aisha said that one morning the Prophet ﷺ went out wearing a striped cloak of black camel hair. Hasan came, and he took him under it; then Husayn; then Fatima; then Ali. Then he said what Allah says in 33:33: “Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity [of sin], O people of the [Prophet’s] household, and to purify you with [extensive] purification” (Muslim 2424).

In the verses of Surat al-Ahzab, this ayah comes among the verses to the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. The hadith shows that his family (Ahl al-Bayt) includes more than the wives, and the Prophet ﷺ prayed for them as his own household.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The explanation of who Ahl al-Bayt includes differs in detail among scholars. Please check how it should be worded for beginners.

steps.title: His family and us
body: The Prophet ﷺ gave a sermon at a watering place named Khumm. He said that he was leaving two weighty things: the Book of Allah, to hold fast to, and the members of his household. He said: “I remind you of your duties to the members of my family” (Muslim 2408).
So Muslims love and respect the family of the Prophet ﷺ. This does not mean that any person is above the rules of Allah. It means we speak of them with respect and care.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The sentence about respect without elevating anyone is the usual Sunni summary. Please confirm.

steps.title: The secret that made her weep and laugh
body: In his last illness, the Prophet ﷺ called Fatima and told her something in secret, and she wept. He told her something else, and she laughed. Aisha asked her about it, and she said: “I would never disclose the secret of Allah’s Messenger ﷺ” (Bukhari 3623; Muslim 2450).

After he died, she told Aisha. He had said that Jibril used to review the Qur’an with him once a year, but that year he reviewed it twice, and he thought this meant his death was near, and that she would be the first of his family to follow him. She wept. Then he said: “Do you not like to be the chief of the women of Paradise, or the chief of the believing women?” She laughed (Bukhari 3623, 3624; Muslim 2450).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Keeping a secret
body: Fatima kept the Prophet’s ﷺ secret while he was alive. She told it only after he died, when Aisha asked her to.
She is also an example of how to carry sorrow and joy together. Aisha said she had never seen happiness so near to sadness as she saw that day (Bukhari 3623).
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: When he died
body: When the Prophet’s ﷺ illness grew heavy and he became unconscious, Fatima said: “How distressed my father is!” He said: “Your father will have no more distress after today” (Bukhari 4462).

When he died she said: “O Father! Who has responded to the call of the Lord Who has invited him! O Father, whose dwelling place is the Garden of Paradise! O Father! We convey this news of your death to Jibril.” When he was buried, she said to Anas: “Do you feel pleased to throw earth over the Messenger of Allah?” (Bukhari 4462).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Grief that is allowed
body: Fatima wept, spoke of her father with love, and asked Anas how hearts could bear to bury him. The sunnah allows weeping and does not allow wailing (see the lesson on grief).
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: A reflection on the words of Fatima in Bukhari 4462. Please confirm.

lessons.title: Hafsa: keeper of the pages
lessons.intro: Learn how Hafsa came to marry the Prophet ﷺ and how the pages of the Qur’an collected for Abu Bakr were kept with her.

steps.title: Hafsa, the daughter of Umar
body: Hafsa bint Umar was the daughter of Umar ibn al-Khattab and a wife of the Prophet ﷺ. Two reports tell her story: how she came to be married to him, and how the first written copy of the Qur’an was kept with her.
Both reports are in Sahih al-Bukhari, so we can tell them with confidence.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A widow and three men
body: Hafsa’s husband, Khunays ibn Hudhafa, one of the Companions, died in Madinah. Her father Umar offered her in marriage first to Uthman, who said he would think about it and later said he did not want to marry at present. Then Umar offered her to Abu Bakr, who stayed silent. Umar was more upset with Abu Bakr than with Uthman (Bukhari 5122).
A few days later the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked for her hand, and Umar married her to him (Bukhari 5122).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Why Abu Bakr was silent
body: Abu Bakr later met Umar and said: nothing stopped him from answering except that he knew the Prophet ﷺ had mentioned Hafsa, and he did not want to let out the secret of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He added that if the Prophet ﷺ had refused her, he would have accepted (Bukhari 5122).
So Abu Bakr bore his friend’s anger rather than break a trust. He kept the Prophet’s secret even at some cost to himself.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A father’s worry
body: Umar was worried about his widowed daughter and went to the men he trusted most. He did not wait for a suitor to arrive. He acted for her.
This is a reflection on the report. It does not say that this is a ruling or an obligation.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: After the battle of Yamama
body: After many reciters of the Qur’an were killed at the battle of Yamama, Umar went to Abu Bakr and said he feared that more would be killed in other battles, and a large part of the Qur’an might be lost. He proposed that the Qur’an be collected (Bukhari 4986).

Abu Bakr said to Zayd ibn Thabit: “You are a wise young man and we do not suspect you, and you used to write the revelation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” Zayd, who wrote the revelation for the Prophet ﷺ, was told to look for the Qur’an and collect it. He said: “How can you do something which Allah’s Messenger ﷺ did not do?” (Bukhari 4986).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The collecting
body: Zayd said that if they had ordered him to move a mountain, it would not have been heavier for him than to collect the Qur’an. In the end, Allah opened his chest to it. He collected the Qur’an from what was written on palm stalks, thin white stones, and from the men who knew it by heart, until he found the last verses of Surat at-Tawbah with Abu Khuzayma al-Ansari, and found them with nobody else (Bukhari 4986).
Then the pages stayed with Abu Bakr until he died, then with Umar until his death, and then with Hafsa, the daughter of Umar (Bukhari 4986).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Uthman asks Hafsa
body: Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman came to Uthman at a time of war in the north. He saw that people were differing about how the Qur’an was recited, and said: “Save this nation before they differ about the Book as the Jews and Christians did before” (Bukhari 4987).

Uthman sent word to Hafsa: “Send us the manuscripts so that we may make perfect copies, and return them to you.” Hafsa sent them. Uthman had Zayd ibn Thabit and three men of Quraysh write out copies, and when they had finished, he returned the original pages to Hafsa. He sent a copy to each province (Bukhari 4987).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Allah’s promise
steps.note: Allah says that it is He who sent down the Qur’an and He will be its guardian. The people in these reports were the means He used.

steps.title: The chain of trust
body: The pages went from Zayd to Abu Bakr, then to Umar, then to Hafsa, then to Uthman, and back to Hafsa. For a time, the pages from which the Qur’an was copied were kept in the house of a woman.
Every time we open a mushaf, we depend on the care of these people, including Hafsa.

steps.text: Treat what is entrusted to you as a trust, not a possession.
steps.detail: Hafsa gave the pages when asked and got them back (Bukhari 4987).

Do not be too proud to ask for a second opinion.

lessons.title: Umm Ayman: the one who raised him
lessons.intro: Learn what the hadith collections report about Umm Ayman, who cared for the Prophet ﷺ, and what she wept for.

steps.title: The woman who nursed him
body: Umm Ayman (also written Umm Aiman) is remembered as the woman who cared for the Prophet ﷺ when he was a child. In Muslim 1771, Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri says that she was an Abyssinian slave of Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet’s ﷺ father, and that she nursed the Prophet ﷺ until he grew up. He later freed her and married her to Zayd ibn Haritha. Their son was Usama (Muslim 1771).
These words are Ibn Shihab’s comment on the hadith, and are not the Prophet’s own words. Other early books say more about her; this lesson keeps to what the hadith collections report.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: He went to see her
body: Anas said that the Prophet ﷺ went to Umm Ayman, and Anas went with him. She offered him a drink in a vessel. He refused it, and the narrator did not know whether it was because he was fasting or for another reason. She raised her voice and showed annoyance with him (Muslim 2453).
She spoke to him as one speaks to a person one has raised. And he visited her, as he did.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The date palms
body: Some of the Ansar had given the Prophet ﷺ date palm trees, and he had given them to Umm Ayman. After Banu Quraydha and Banu an-Nadir were conquered, the Ansar asked for their trees back. Anas’s people sent him to ask the Prophet ﷺ (Bukhari 4120).

Umm Ayman put the garment around Anas’s neck and said: “No, by Him except Whom none has the right to be worshipped, he will not return those trees to you, as he has given them to me.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “Return those trees and I will give you so much instead.” She kept refusing, until he had given her ten times the number of her date palms (Bukhari 4120; Muslim 1771).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: His patience with her
body: The Prophet ﷺ did not tell her off. He offered more, and again more, until she was content.
This is a reflection on the report, and it is not a ruling.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: The visit after he died
body: After the death of the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr said to Umar: “Let us visit Umm Ayman, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit her.” When they came to her, she wept. They said: “What makes you weep? What is in store for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with Allah is better.”

She said: “I do not weep because I do not know that what is in store for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is better, but because the revelation from heaven has ceased.” This moved both of them to tears and they began to weep along with her (Muslim 2454).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What she missed
body: Umm Ayman did not weep only for the man. She wept for the voice of Allah, which came to the world through him and then stopped. She understood what had been lost to the world.
We still have the Qur’an. It is the revelation that continues to speak to us, and we can open it any day.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Love for her family
body: Ibn Umar once saw Hajjaj, the son of Umm Ayman, pray without completing his bowing and prostration. He told him to repeat the prayer. Afterwards he said: “If Allah’s Messenger ﷺ saw him, he would have loved him”, and mentioned the Prophet’s ﷺ love for the children of Umm Ayman (Bukhari 3737).
Two things appear here: love for her family, and a call to pray properly, even when a person is dear to us.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What we do not claim
body: Other books report that she gave water to fighters at Uhud, that she wept at the Prophet’s ﷺ death in a way that Ibn Sa’d describes, and that the Prophet ﷺ called her “mother” and said she was the rest of his household. We did not find these in the hadith collections we checked.

The sources also give different dates for her death: Muslim 1771 has Ibn Shihab saying she died five months after the Prophet ﷺ, while some other books give a later time. We do not choose between them here.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.source: Muslim 1771; Ibn Sa’d, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8 pp. 223-226 (not from the six books)

lessons.title: Sumayyah: patience when few
lessons.intro: Learn about the early believers who were tested in Makkah and about Sumayyah, with a clear line between what is sourced and what is a seerah report.

steps.title: When there were few believers
body: Ammar ibn Yasir, who was the son of Sumayyah, said: “I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the only ones who had accepted Islam with him were five slaves, two women and Abu Bakr” (Bukhari 3857).
Early Islam was weak in numbers and in power. This lesson is about the believers who held on in those years, and about one woman in particular, Sumayyah bint Khayyat.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Faith is tested
body: Allah says: “Do the people think that they will be left to say, «We believe» and they will not be tried?” (29:2). And: “But We have certainly tried those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars” (29:3).
Allah also says: “O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient” (2:153).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Khabbab complains to the Prophet ﷺ
body: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: “We complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of the persecution of the unbelievers while he was sitting in the shade of the Ka’bah, leaning on his cloak. We said: «Will you not seek help for us? Will you not pray to Allah for us?»” (Bukhari 3612).

He said that among the nations before them, a believer would be put in a pit that was dug for him and sawn in two, yet that would not turn him from his religion; his flesh would be combed from his bones with iron combs, yet that would not make him leave his religion. He said that Allah would complete this matter until a rider could travel from Sana to Hadramawt fearing none but Allah, “but you are hasty” (Bukhari 3612).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Sumayyah
body: Sumayyah bint Khayyat was the mother of Ammar and the wife of Yasir. The seerah books (Ibn Sa’d, Ibn Hisham) report that she was a slave woman of Banu Makhzum, that her family became Muslim early, and that they were tortured by the clan.

Ibn Ishaq says the Prophet ﷺ would pass by them and say: “Be patient, family of Yasir, for your meeting place is Paradise.” He reports that Sumayyah was killed because she would accept nothing but Islam, and that she is called the first martyr in Islam.

These are seerah reports from books that are not among the six hadith collections. They come without a full chain in the pages we checked, and have not yet been reviewed by a scholar. We hold them as reports and not as established facts.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.source: Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya, vol. 1 pp. 317-320; Ibn Sa’d, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 3 pp. 233, 246 (seerah; not from the six books)
steps.review: All Sumayyah details here come from Ibn Hisham and Ibn Sa’d only (her being a slave, the torture, the words of the Prophet ﷺ, her death, being the first martyr). Please confirm the wording or remove.

steps.title: What the hadith collections do say about her son
body: Ammar ibn Yasir is named in Sahih al-Bukhari as one of the early Muslims in Makkah (3857). Bukhari 3287 records that Abu ad-Darda said Ammar was the person whom Allah protected against Satan through the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ.
Ammar later reached Madinah among the first Companions who came there after Mus’ab ibn Umayr and Ibn Umm Maktum (Bukhari 3924).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The ruling on being forced
body: Allah says of those who disbelieve after belief, “except for one who is forced [to renounce his religion] while his heart is secure in faith” (16:106). So a person who is forced to say words of disbelief under torture, while his heart remains at peace in faith, is not blamed.
The Qur’an does not tell us who this verse was revealed about. Some books of tafsir link it to Ammar ibn Yasir. We do not rely on that link here.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The statement that the verse is linked to Ammar in some tafsir books is mentioned only to say it is not relied on. Please confirm the wording.

steps.title: What her story asks of us
body: Whatever the details, the lesson is clear and it is sourced elsewhere: the first Muslims were tested, Allah is with the patient, and the religion spread because people held on.
We do not face the sand of Makkah. We face smaller tests: mockery, pressure to hide our faith, pressure to give up a prayer. The same patience and prayer is what Allah asked for (2:153).

lessons.title: Nusaybah and the women of Uhud
lessons.intro: Learn what the hadith books say about women who helped at Uhud, and meet Nusaybah through the seerah.

steps.title: Women on the battlefield, as helpers
body: Nusaybah bint Ka’b, known as Umm Ammarah, is remembered by the seerah books as an Ansari woman who was at the pledge of Aqabah and at Uhud. Those details come from Ibn Sa’d and Ibn Hisham and are not in the six hadith books, so we hold them as reports and have asked a scholar to review them.
This lesson teaches what the hadith books themselves say about women who helped in the early battles, and then names her.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.source: Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (Uhud); Ibn Sa’d, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8 (seerah; not from the six books)
steps.review: All Nusaybah-specific details (the pledge of Aqabah, Uhud, her wounds) are seerah-only. Please confirm or remove.

steps.title: Uhud: water and wounds
body: Anas said: “On the day of Uhud, when some people turned away and left the Prophet ﷺ, I saw Aisha bint Abu Bakr and Umm Sulaym with their robes tucked up, hurrying with water skins. They poured water into the mouths of the people, went back to fill the skins and came back again” (Bukhari 2880).
Ar-Rubayyi bint Mu’awwidh said: “We were with the Prophet ﷺ giving water to the wounded, treating them, and carrying the dead back to Madinah” (Bukhari 2882).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What Ibn Abbas wrote
body: A man named Najda asked Ibn Abbas whether the Prophet ﷺ took women to battle and gave them a share of the booty. Ibn Abbas wrote that he did take them, that they treated the wounded, and that they were given a reward from the booty, but no regular share was assigned to them (Muslim 1812).
He also wrote that the Prophet ﷺ did not kill the children of the enemy (Muslim 1812). The role of women was care for the wounded, water and support.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Nusaybah in the reports
body: The seerah books say that Nusaybah fought to protect the Prophet ﷺ at Uhud and was wounded many times, and that he praised her. They also say that her husband and her sons were with her.
We do not repeat the wording of those reports here, because we have not checked them in the six hadith books. If you want to read them, read them in Ibn Hisham with a teacher.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: These are seerah claims. Please review before they are kept.

steps.title: Women pledged to the Prophet ﷺ too
body: Allah says that when believing women come to the Prophet to pledge, they are not to associate anything with Allah, steal, commit unlawful sex, kill their children, forge lies or disobey him in what is right (60:12).
Aisha said he would take their pledge by words, and “by Allah, his hand never touched a woman’s hand during that pledge”. He would say: “I have accepted your pledge” (Bukhari 4891).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What this shows
body: In the first community, women were present at the hardest moments, giving water and treating wounds. They were also full members of the community, who pledged to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ directly.
The scholars differ on what women may do in fighting today. This lesson does not give a ruling on that; ask a scholar of your school.

lessons.title: Khawlah: Allah heard her
lessons.intro: Learn how a woman’s complaint to the Prophet ﷺ and to Allah led to the opening of Surah Al-Mujadilah.

steps.title: A woman who spoke up
body: Khawlah bint Tha’labah was the wife of Aws ibn as-Samit. Aisha said that Khawlah complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about her husband, and she kept complaining to Allah until Jibril brought down verses of the Qur’an (Ibn Majah 2063; 188, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).
The chapter that begins with her story is named Al-Mujadilah, “The Woman Who Disputes”.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Ibn Majah 2063 and 188, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai

steps.title: What Aisha heard
body: Aisha said: “Blessed is the One Whose hearing encompasses all things. I heard some of the words of Khawlah bint Tha’labah, but some of her words were not clear to me.” Khawlah said her husband had “consumed my youth”, that she had borne him children, and that when she grew old he declared zihar upon her. She said: “O Allah, I complain to You” (Ibn Majah 2063, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).
In another narration Aisha says she was in a corner of the house and could not hear what the woman said, yet Allah revealed the verse (Ibn Majah 188, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Ibn Majah 2063 and 188, sahih per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai

steps.title: Allah heard her
body: Allah says: “Certainly has Allah heard the speech of the one who argues with you, [O Muhammad], concerning her husband and directs her complaint to Allah. And Allah hears your dialogue; indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing” (58:1).
The verse tells us that Allah heard a woman complain, and that her complaint changed a law for everyone after her.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What zihar is
body: Zihar is when a man says to his wife something like “you are to me like my mother’s back”. It was an old practice in Arabia, used to leave a wife in limbo.

Allah says that those who say this: “they are not [consequently] their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they are saying an objectionable statement and a falsehood” (58:2).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The way out
body: Allah gives a way out, in order: “then [there must be] the freeing of a slave before they touch one another” (58:3). “And he who does not find [a slave] - then a fast for two months consecutively before they touch one another; and he who is unable - then the feeding of sixty poor persons” (58:4).
The scholars of all four schools take the three steps as an order: free a slave, then fast two months in a row, then feed sixty poor people. Please take a real case to a scholar of your school.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The statement that all four schools take the three steps in order and that the fast is consecutive should be confirmed. Details such as how much food each person gets differ and are not given here.

steps.title: The story as told to the Prophet ﷺ
body: Another report names the wife as Khuwaylah, daughter of Malik ibn Tha’labah, and tells how she went through the three steps with the Prophet ﷺ. This report carries different grades from different scholars, so we do not rely on its details here.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.source: Abu Dawud (report graded differently by different scholars; not relied on)
steps.review: A report on the same event in Abu Dawud is graded hasan by one scholar and daif by another, so its details (the basket of dates, her offering to help) are left out. Please confirm.

steps.title: What it teaches
body: She brought a hard personal matter to the Prophet ﷺ and to Allah, and she did not stop. Allah’s answer protected every woman after her.
Speaking to Allah about a hurt is not rude. It is dua. Speaking up to the right people when you are wronged is also allowed.

lessons.title: Asma: two belts and a kind heart
lessons.intro: Learn about Asma bint Abu Bakr: the hijrah journey food, her hard work, and her kindness to her mother.

steps.title: The owner of two belts
body: Asma bint Abu Bakr was the daughter of Abu Bakr as-Siddiq and the older sister of Aisha. She married az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam.
She is known as Dhat an-Nitaqayn, “the owner of two belts”. This lesson tells why, how she lived with az-Zubayr, and how she treated her mother who was not a Muslim.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The journey food
body: Asma said: “I prepared the journey food for the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr when they wanted to migrate to Madinah. I said to my father: «I do not have anything to tie the container of the journey food with except my waist belt.» He said: «Divide it lengthwise into two.» I did so, and for this reason I was named Dhat an-Nitaqayn” (Bukhari 3907).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A small thing in a big journey
body: The hijrah changed history. Asma’s part was food and a belt. She did what was in her hand, at once, and it is remembered.
Not every good act is large. Most are done with what you have in the moment.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Her work at home
body: Asma said: when az-Zubayr married her he had no property, no slave and nothing but a camel that drew water and his horse. She fed the horse, drew water, sewed the bucket and made dough, but she did not know how to bake bread, so her Ansari neighbours baked for her. She carried date stones on her head from the land the Prophet ﷺ had given az-Zubayr, about two-thirds of a farsakh from her house (Bukhari 5224).

One day the Prophet ﷺ met her with some of the Ansar and made his camel kneel so she could ride behind him. She felt shy and remembered az-Zubayr’s sense of ghira (protective jealousy), and the Prophet ﷺ saw this and went on. Az-Zubayr said: “By Allah, your carrying the date stones is more shameful to me than your riding with him” (Bukhari 5224).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What her work shows
body: She was a hard worker in a poor home. The hadith tells us she was patient, that the neighbours helped her, and that her father later sent a servant, “as if he had set me free”.
The report also shows the Prophet ﷺ noticing her shyness and moving on, and a husband’s honest feelings.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Her mother
body: Asma said: “My mother came to me during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, and she was a pagan. I asked the Prophet ﷺ: «My mother has come to me and she wants something from me. Shall I keep good relations with her?» He said: «Yes, keep good relations with her»” (Bukhari 2620).
In another narration she says her mother came “hoping for my favour”, and Ibn Uyaynah says that the verse was revealed then (Bukhari 5978).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The verse
body: Allah says: “Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly” (60:8).
The link between this verse and Asma’s mother is made by a narrator (Ibn Uyaynah), not by the Prophet ﷺ, so we say so.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The wording that the verse was revealed about Asma’s mother is a narrator’s statement. Please confirm that this is how the text should be put.

steps.text: Be kind in words and in manner.

lessons.title: Umm Salama: words in grief, advice in a crisis
lessons.intro: Learn what Umm Salama said after the loss of her husband, and her advice to the Prophet ﷺ at Hudaybiyyah.

steps.title: A widow, a wife and a counsellor
body: Umm Salama (Hind bint Abi Umayyah) was married to Abu Salama. When he died, she became a wife of the Prophet ﷺ. Muslim 918 gives her own account of that time. Another hadith, Bukhari 2731, shows her giving advice at a critical moment.
This lesson takes those two reports.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What she said after Abu Salama died
steps.note: Umm Salama reported that the Prophet ﷺ said that any Muslim struck by a calamity who says these words will be given something better in exchange. When Abu Salama died she asked herself what Muslim could be better than Abu Salama, yet she said the words as she was told, and Allah gave her the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in exchange (Muslim 918).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Saying it when it is hard to believe
body: She said she did not think anyone was better than Abu Salama, and still she said the words. She did not wait to feel ready.
Words said in grief are an act of worship even when the heart is heavy. The hadith does not say she felt no pain.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: The proposal
body: She said the Prophet ﷺ sent Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah with a message of marriage. She replied that she had a daughter to look after and was of a jealous nature. The Prophet ﷺ said: as for her daughter, we will ask Allah to free her of the responsibility, and as for the jealousy, he would ask Allah to take it away (Muslim 918).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The day of Hudaybiyyah
body: After the treaty was written, the Prophet ﷺ told the Companions: “Get up and slaughter your sacrifices and get your head shaved.” None of them got up, and he repeated it three times. He went to Umm Salama and told her how the people felt (Bukhari 2731).

She said: “O Prophet of Allah ﷺ! Do you want your order to be carried out? Go out and do not say a word to anybody until you have slaughtered your sacrifice and call your barber to shave your head.” He did, and when they saw it, the Companions got up, slaughtered their sacrifices and began to shave one another’s heads (Bukhari 2731).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What her counsel shows
body: The Prophet ﷺ went to his wife for counsel at a hard moment, and he acted on her advice. The hadith records this without comment.
It shows that a woman’s advice was sought and used at a decisive moment for the community. Some scholars add more to this lesson; the hadith gives us the event.

lessons.title: Zaynab bint Jahsh: the long hand
lessons.intro: Learn about Zaynab bint Jahsh: her charity, the choice Allah gave the wives, and Aisha’s praise of her.

steps.title: The one who gave in charity
body: Zaynab bint Jahsh was a wife of the Prophet ﷺ. Aisha, who was her rival in some moments, gave this description of her in Muslim 2442: “I have never seen a woman more advanced in religious piety than Zaynab, more God-conscious, more truthful, more alive to the ties of blood, more generous and having more sense of self-sacrifice in practical life and having more charitable disposition.”
That is Aisha’s own judgement of her, and it is in Sahih Muslim.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The longest hand
body: Aisha reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: “One who has the longest hands among you will meet me most immediately.” His wives used to measure their hands, and the hand of Zaynab was the longest, “as she used to work with her hand and spend that income on charity” (Muslim 2452).
Bukhari 1420 gives the same saying. There, the wives measured with a stick, and it was only after Zaynab bint Jahsh died first that they understood the long hand was a symbol of giving in charity.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What the long hand means
body: The Prophet ﷺ was speaking about generosity, and the wives understood that only after Zaynab died. So the first meaning is a lesson on giving.
Zaynab earned by her own hands and gave away what she earned. The lesson is not only for rich people: it is for anyone who has work.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The choice Allah gave the wives
body: Allah told the Prophet ﷺ to say to his wives: “If you should desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and give you a gracious release. But if you should desire Allah and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter - then indeed, Allah has prepared for the doers of good among you a great reward” (33:28-29).
Zaynab and the other wives chose Allah and His Messenger.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The last sentence says the wives chose Allah and His Messenger. This is the well-known account, but it was not checked verse by verse here. Please confirm.

steps.title: Her marriage and a custom ended
body: Anas said that the verse of 33:37, about what the Prophet ﷺ kept hidden within himself and Allah was to disclose, was revealed about Zaynab bint Jahsh and Zayd ibn Haritha (Bukhari 4787).

Allah says the marriage was done “in order that there not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer have need of them” (33:37). That is, it ended a custom that treated an adopted son as a real son in marriage law.
The Qur’an and hadith here are brief, and we do not add details from later books.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The explanation of the custom ends with the sense of the verse only. Other details of this event are left out on purpose. Please confirm.

steps.title: Her honesty with her rival
body: The Prophet’s ﷺ wives sent Fatima to ask for fairness in the affection shown to Aisha. When it did not work, they sent Zaynab. She spoke harshly to Aisha. Aisha waited until she saw the Prophet ﷺ would not mind, then answered back until Zaynab was quiet. He smiled and said: “She is the daughter of Abu Bakr” (Muslim 2442).
Even in the very report where Aisha says Zaynab “lost temper very soon but was soon calm”, she praises her.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What to take from her
body: She worked, she gave, she chose Allah, and she was honest. The person closest to her in rank spoke the highest praise of her after an argument.
The way we describe people we disagree with says something about us.

lessons.title: Juwayriyya: freedom and four words
lessons.intro: Learn how Juwayriyya was freed, and the dhikr the Prophet ﷺ taught her.

steps.title: Juwayriyya bint al-Harith
body: Juwayriyya was the daughter of al-Harith, chief of Banu al-Mustaliq. Aisha reported that she fell to the lot of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas (or to his cousin) and made an agreement to buy her freedom (Abu Dawud 3931, hasan per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).
This lesson takes two reports about her: how she was freed, and a dhikr she was taught.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Abu Dawud 3931, hasan per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai

steps.title: She asks for help to buy her freedom
body: Aisha said that Juwayriyya came to the door and asked the Prophet ﷺ for help with the price of her freedom. She said: “Messenger of Allah, I am Juwayriyya, daughter of al-Harith, and something has happened to me which is not hidden from you.” He said: “Are you inclined to that which is better?” She asked what that was. He said: “I shall pay the price of your freedom on your behalf, and I shall marry you.” She said: “I shall do this” (Abu Dawud 3931, hasan per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).

When the people heard that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had married her, they released the captives they held, saying they were now his relatives by marriage. Aisha said: “We did not see any woman greater than Juwayriyya who brought blessings to her people. One hundred families of Banu al-Mustaliq were set free on account of her” (Abu Dawud 3931, hasan per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai).
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Abu Dawud 3931, hasan per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai

steps.title: What this report shows
body: Freeing a person by agreement (mukataba) was a known route to freedom. The Prophet ﷺ offered her something better than the price, and many others were freed because of that.
Aisha, who was not happy at first when she saw her at the door, still gave her the highest praise afterwards. Honest speech and fair judgement go together.
steps.label: [Reflection]
steps.source: Abu Dawud 3931, hasan per al-Albani and Zubair Ali Zai

steps.title: What the seerah books add
body: Seerah books such as Ibn Hisham tell the story of the Banu al-Mustaliq expedition in more detail, and give a different account of how she was freed. We do not use those details here.
Where the books differ with the hadith, we keep to the hadith we have checked.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The seerah accounts of this event are not repeated. Please confirm that nothing further is needed.

steps.title: Sitting in her place of prayer
body: Juwayriyya reported that the Prophet ﷺ went out from her in the morning while she was in her place of prayer after the dawn prayer. He came back in the forenoon and she was still sitting there. He said: “You have been in the same place since I left you.” She said: “Yes” (Muslim 2726).
He said: “I recited four words three times after I left you, and if they were weighed against what you have said since this morning, they would outweigh it” (Muslim 2726).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The four words
steps.note: This is the dhikr the Prophet ﷺ taught Juwayriyya, as reported in Muslim 2726. The Prophet ﷺ said he said these words three times. You can say it after the dawn prayer or at any time.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The Arabic is copied from Muslim 2726. The statement that you can say it at any time is common teaching, not stated as a rule in the hadith. Please confirm.

steps.title: What it means
body: It says: glory be to Allah and praise to Him, by the number of His creation, the pleasure of Himself, the weight of His Throne and the ink of His words.
The idea is that your praise is not limited by what you can count. The words call on a number no one can count.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Adding the dhikr to your morning

steps.text: After the dawn prayer, stay a little in your place.
Say the words with the meaning in mind.
Say it three times, as the Prophet ﷺ said he did.
Do not worry about how long you stay; the hadith does not set a time.

mistakes: Saying the words fast without thinking of the meaning.
Counting loudly to show others.

lessons.title: Safiyya: care and closing the door on doubt
lessons.intro: Learn how the Prophet ﷺ treated Safiyya, and what the mosque scene teaches about suspicion.

steps.title: Safiyya bint Huyayy
body: Safiyya bint Huyayy was a wife of the Prophet ﷺ. Her father, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, was of the Jewish tribe of Banu an-Nadir. Anas reported that she was among the captives after Khaybar, that she first came to the share of Dihya al-Kalbi and then belonged to the Prophet ﷺ, and that he made her freedom her mahr (Bukhari 4200).
This lesson takes what the hadith books say about how she was treated and what she taught about avoiding suspicion.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: On the road to Madinah
body: Anas said that the Prophet ﷺ married her on the way, and that a meal of hais (a date dish) was prepared as the wedding banquet. Then, on the way to Madinah, “I saw the Prophet ﷺ making for her a kind of cushion with his cloak behind him on his camel. He then sat beside his camel and put his knee for Safiyya to put her foot on, in order to ride” (Bukhari 4211).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What this shows
body: A widow who had lost her family was treated with care: a cushion, a knee to step on, a shared meal. The hadith does not tell us what she felt, and we do not guess.
It also shows that the Prophet ﷺ married her after he freed her, and did not keep her as a captive.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: In the mosque during itikaf
body: Safiyya said she went to visit the Prophet ﷺ in the mosque while he was in itikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan. She talked with him for a while, then got up to go home, and he went with her. At the gate of the mosque, two men of the Ansar passed and greeted him (Bukhari 2035).

He said to them: “Do not run away! She is my wife, Safiyya bint Huyayy.” They said: “Subhan Allah, O Messenger of Allah!” and it was hard on them. He said: “Satan reaches everywhere in the human body as blood reaches in it. I was afraid lest Satan put an evil thought in your minds” (Bukhari 2035).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Closing the door on suspicion
body: He did not wait to be accused. He stopped the two men and told them who she was, to protect them from a doubt and to protect her from it.
We can follow this: if a thing could look wrong to a fair-minded person, we can explain it kindly and early.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The practical lesson (explaining early what could be misread) is drawn by scholars from this hadith; it is not stated as a ruling. Please confirm.

steps.title: A note about itikaf
body: The hadith shows that the person in itikaf may speak with a visitor, and may go to the gate of the mosque with her. Scholars of the different schools give further rules on what breaks itikaf and what does not, which are not given here.
If you plan to make itikaf, ask a scholar of your school.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The schools differ on the details of itikaf. This note only refers you to a teacher and does not rule. Please confirm.

steps.title: A report we do not use
body: Some books tell of Safiyya being taunted as the daughter of a Jew, and of the Prophet ﷺ telling her what to answer. The report is graded weak in the Tirmidhi collection, so we do not use it as a lesson.
We keep to sound reports and say so when we leave one out.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The weak report is only mentioned as not used. Please confirm that no number is needed.

mistakes: Waiting until you are accused.

lessons.title: The queen of Sheba: consult and submit
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an says about the queen of Sheba and what it does not say.

steps.title: The queen of Sheba
body: The Qur’an tells of a woman who ruled the people of Sheba (Saba). Her name is not given in the Qur’an. Later books call her Bilqis, but we do not rely on that name here.
Her story is in Surah An-Naml, 27:20-44. This lesson teaches what the verses say about her, and not what later books add.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The statement that her name is not given in the Qur’an and that later books call her Bilqis is general knowledge, and no book is cited. Please confirm.

steps.title: The report that reached Sulayman
body: A hoopoe came to Sulayman (Solomon) and said: “Indeed, I found [there] a woman ruling them, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne” (27:23).
It also said that she and her people prostrated to the sun instead of Allah (27:24). The Qur’an states this plainly. The bird’s report is true, and it led to the letter that follows.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The sentence that the bird’s report is true is a note on the narrative; the Qur’an does not say it in these words. Please confirm.

steps.title: The letter
body: The queen said to her chiefs: «O eminent ones, indeed, to me has been delivered a noble letter. Indeed, it is from Solomon, and indeed, it reads: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful» (27:29-30).
She called it “noble”. She took the letter seriously and read it out to her council, instead of dismissing it.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: She asks for advice
body: She said to them: «O eminent ones, advise me in my affair. I would not decide a matter until you witness [for] me» (27:32).
They answered that they were men of strength and great military might, “but the command is yours, so see what you will command” (27:33).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: She chooses caution over war
body: She said: «Indeed kings - when they enter a city, they ruin it and render the honored of its people humbled. And thus do they do» (27:34).
Then she said she would send a gift and see with what reply the messengers returned (27:35). She chose to test the matter before choosing war.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Where she ends
body: After she saw the palace of Sulayman, she said: «My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to Allah, Lord of the worlds» (27:44).
The account ends with her submission to Allah. She is not described by the Qur’an as a villain; she is described as a ruler who listened, thought and then turned to Allah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What the Qur’an does not say
body: Many later stories about her (her appearance, her family, her marriage, her throne’s details) come from books outside the Qur’an. We do not repeat them, because we have not been able to check them against the hadith collections.
The verses give us what we need: a ruler who consults, who is careful, and who submits to the truth.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.source: Not found in the six books; not used
steps.review: The statement that later stories are not checked against the hadith collections is a note of method. Please confirm.

steps.title: Lessons for a leader at home or at work
body: Take a message seriously. Ask others before deciding. Choose a path that costs fewer lives. Be ready to say “I wronged myself” when the truth is clear.

These are lessons drawn from the verses. They are not rulings. Whether a woman may lead a state is a question that scholars have discussed using other texts, and it is not decided by this story; ask a scholar if you need to know.
steps.label: [Reflection]
steps.review: The note that scholars have discussed women leading a state is a pointer only. Please confirm or give the schools.

steps.title: Deciding with others

steps.text: Read the whole message before you react.
Ask the people who will be affected.
Weigh the cost of each path.
Test before you commit.
When the truth is clear, say so and turn to Allah.

mistakes: Deciding alone when others are affected.
